title: Book Three · Chapter 4: Into the Post Box
story:
On the second morning, Ronan puts the letter in his bag. He puts it inside a book. The book keeps the envelope flat.

At school, he takes out the book.

“Is that homework?” Anna asks.

“A letter. My friend lives in another city now.”

“Are you taking it to the post office?”

“After school. With Mum.”

He puts the book back. The teacher comes in, and Anna opens her exercise book.

All afternoon, the envelope stays between the pages. At the last bell, Ronan checks it once. There is a small blue mark near the corner. His pen has no cap.

He finds the cap at the bottom of his bag. Then he puts everything away.

Mum waits outside the school gate. Her work basket hangs from one arm.

“Did the coat go?” he asks.

“Yes. The pocket is in use already.”

“What did the customer put in it?”

“Her keys. She checked before she left.”

They walk to the post office. Mum needs a packet of needles too. The little shop beside the post office sells them.

Inside the post office, three people stand in front of Ronan. A man holds a brown parcel. A woman has several envelopes.

Ronan takes his own letter out of the book. He holds it with both hands.

Mum looks at the blue mark.

“Is that part of the address?”

“No. My pen did that.”

“Then your pen wants to write to Leo too.”

Their turn comes. Ronan puts the envelope on the counter.

“One stamp, please.”

The woman behind the counter looks at the envelope. She tells him the price. He takes the money from his pocket and gives it to her.

She gives him a stamp and some change.

“Top right,” she says.

Ronan presses the stamp onto the envelope. One corner lifts. He presses that corner again.

Mum steps aside. Another customer moves to the counter.

Outside, Ronan stops at the post box. He holds the envelope near the opening.

He can still take it home. He can add another joke or make the drawing better.

“Ready?” Mum asks.

“Yes.”

He pushes the letter through. It drops inside with a soft sound.

His hand comes back empty.

For a moment, he looks at the narrow opening. Then Mum lifts her basket.

“Now the needles.”

In the little shop, she asks for two different sizes. Ronan holds the basket while she chooses.

On the way home, he puts his hand inside the book again. Only the pages are there.

“You sent it,” Mum says.

“I know. My hand doesn't know yet.”

She smiles. At the next corner, they buy vegetables for dinner. Ronan carries the heavier bag. The empty place in his school book stays empty all the way home.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

flat＝平整的；counter＝柜台；change＝找回的零钱；press＝按、压。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan为什么把信夹进书里？
2. 离开邮局时，第一封信已经在哪里？Mum接着要买什么？

## 读句子

**The book keeps the envelope flat.**

拆开看：The book / keeps the envelope / flat.

书／使信封保持／平整。
